ELI5: Bernie Madoff's ponzi scheme/investment fraud

I say to you, "Give me ten dollars, and I'll give you one dollar a month for the next year."

Normal investing means I take those ten dollars and give it to a business that needs to grow, getting some profit money back in return. But this is not steady, one month the investment gives me 3 dollars back and then for 3 months I get no money back, and have to pay you out of pocket.

With my Ponzi scheme, I take your ten dollars, then think to myself "I'll give him a dollar every month, but from another person's ten dollars." So I find a second person to give me ten dollars, saying the same thing that I said to you. I have to keep finding people to give me money to keep paying now two people, then three, then four, then etc. etc.

Investing is hard because sometimes I have to tell people who gave me money that their investment didn't work out. My Ponzi scheme is attractive because I don't have to tell you bad news (because I'm lying), and because you get a dollar back every month for as long as I keep it up. I can claim it's a risk-free investment.

But in reality, there is no money in a Ponzi scheme, I'm just passing it to the last person I just took it from. Like musical chairs. This works time and time again because people don't like risk, and it seems like a really consistent investment. It fails every time because it runs out of money. This is what happened with Bernie Madoff.

To add to /u/your_grammers_bad's explaination of a ponzi, Madoff sold his investors that he was so well connected, he could front run option markets and make a mint (basically he's giving his investors a way to extract profits from essentially everyone else). This has nothing to do with the ponzi (which worked as described), but did provide a huge amount of cover (providing a legit explanation for how his fund could earn 13% in a year when all markets were down 20%) allowing it to get very large and explained his enormous string of positive returns in all markets.
